title: Add a sphere to the document
task: Add a sphere to the active Rhino document with RhinoDoc.Objects.AddSphere and return its object id. Build the Sphere from a centre point and radius, then redraw so it shows in the viewports.
script:
# Task: add a sphere to the active Rhino document and return its object id.
import System
import Rhino
import scriptcontext as sc

# 1. Build the geometry: a sphere centred at the origin, radius 5 (model units).
sphere = Rhino.Geometry.Sphere(Rhino.Geometry.Point3d(0, 0, 0), 5.0)

# 2. Add it to the document. AddSphere bakes the sphere as a surface object and
#    returns its System.Guid -- Guid.Empty means the add failed.
guid = sc.doc.Objects.AddSphere(sphere)
if guid == System.Guid.Empty:
    raise Exception("AddSphere returned an empty id")

# 3. Redraw so the new object shows in the viewports (a script edit does not
#    trigger a redraw on its own).
sc.doc.Views.Redraw()

result = "added sphere %s" % guid

pitfalls.symptom: AddSphere returns and the code runs, but the sphere is not visible in any viewport.
pitfalls.cause: A script does not trigger a viewport redraw on its own; the new object is in the document but the views are stale.
pitfalls.fix: Call sc.doc.Views.Redraw() after adding objects so the viewports repaint.
